ch9.title: Muscles and Muscle Tissue
ch9.status: CURRENT — mish is on this NOW
ch9.covered_so_far: three muscle types through excitation-contraction coupling

smooth.location: walls of hollow organs, vessels, airways

muscle_tissue_types.overlap: all three contract, all generate heat, all need Ca2+ to work. but ONLY skeletal is voluntary + striated + multinucleate.

functions_of_muscle_tissue: 1. MOVEMENT — body movement, breathing, blood circulation, GI propulsion, speech
2. MAINTAIN POSTURE + BODY POSITION — constant tiny contractions hold us upright
3. STABILIZE JOINTS — muscle tone keeps bones aligned
4. GENERATE HEAT — contraction byproduct. shivering = emergency heat production
5. PROTECT ORGANS + GUARD OPENINGS — abdominal muscles, sphincters

four_functional_characteristics.excitability: receives + responds to stimuli (nerve impulses, hormones, stretch)
four_functional_characteristics.elasticity: recoils back to resting length after stretch

connective_tissue_coverings.note: three layers, outside to in. all continuous with each other and with the tendon.
connective_tissue_coverings.epimysium: DENSE irregular CT wrapping the ENTIRE muscle. outermost.
connective_tissue_coverings.perimysium: wraps BUNDLES of muscle fibers called FASCICLES. middle layer.
connective_tissue_coverings.endomysium: fine areolar CT around EACH individual muscle fiber (cell). innermost.

attachments.tendon: rope-like dense regular CT connecting muscle to bone. continuous with periosteum.
attachments.aponeurosis: flat, sheet-like tendon (ex: abdominal aponeuroses, galea aponeurotica of scalp).
attachments.origin: attachment to the LESS movable bone. stays put.
attachments.insertion: attachment to the MORE movable bone. moves TOWARD origin during contraction.

parallel.pattern: fibers run parallel to long axis

fusiform.pattern: parallel but muscle widens in middle

pennate.pattern: fibers meet tendon at an angle

muscle_fiber.what: a single skeletal muscle fiber IS one cell. long, cylindrical, MULTINUCLEATE (nuclei pushed to periphery under sarcolemma). formed by fusion of hundreds of embryonic cells.
muscle_fiber.sarcolemma: plasma membrane of the muscle fiber.
muscle_fiber.sarcoplasm: cytoplasm. contains glycosomes (glycogen) + myoglobin (binds O2, red color).
muscle_fiber.myofibrils: rod-like contractile organelles filling the sarcoplasm. 80% of fiber volume. show striations.
muscle_fiber.sarcoplasmic_reticulum: modified smooth ER wrapping each myofibril. stores + releases Ca2+. terminal cisternae = enlarged ends.
muscle_fiber.t_tubules: inward extensions of the sarcolemma, running deep into the cell at every A-I junction. carry the action potential INTO the fiber.
muscle_fiber.triad: 1 T-tubule flanked by 2 SR terminal cisternae. the Ca2+-release machinery.

sarcomere.what: FUNCTIONAL UNIT of muscle. region of a myofibril from one Z disc to the next. shortens during contraction. ~2 micrometers at rest.
sarcomere.z_disc: boundary between sarcomeres. thin filaments anchor here.
sarcomere.i_band: LIGHT. thin filaments only. gets SHORTER during contraction.
sarcomere.a_band: DARK. full length of thick filaments. STAYS THE SAME LENGTH during contraction. always A-band length.
sarcomere.h_zone: center of A band. thick filaments only (no overlap). DISAPPEARS during contraction.
sarcomere.m_line: center of H zone. anchors thick filaments.
sarcomere.memory_trick: the LIGHT bands shorten, the DARK bands stay. H zone and I band close in on each other. A band is always A band.

myofilaments.thick_myosin: bundled myosin molecules. each has a HEAD (binds actin + ATP, hinged) and a TAIL. heads form CROSS-BRIDGES.

thin_actin.actin: two intertwined strands. each actin monomer has a myosin-binding site.
thin_actin.tropomyosin: rod wrapping around actin. COVERS myosin-binding sites at rest.
thin_actin.troponin: three-subunit complex sitting on tropomyosin. one subunit binds Ca2+.

sliding_filament_theory.principle: muscle shortens because thin filaments slide inward along thick filaments. filaments themselves do NOT change length. only the degree of OVERLAP changes.
sliding_filament_theory.at_rest: thin + thick overlap partially. H zone + I band visible.
sliding_filament_theory.during_contraction: myosin heads grab actin, pull inward toward M line, release, grab again. thin filaments slide toward center of sarcomere.
sliding_filament_theory.result: Z discs pull closer together → sarcomere shortens → whole muscle shortens.

neuromuscular_junction.what: synapse between a motor neuron and a muscle fiber. where 'move' gets delivered.

structure.axon_terminal: ends in synaptic end bulbs with ACh vesicles
structure.motor_end_plate: specialized sarcolemma region, folded, packed with nicotinic ACh receptors

sequence: 1. action potential arrives at axon terminal → voltage-gated Ca2+ channels open → Ca2+ enters terminal
2. Ca2+ triggers ACh release from synaptic vesicles
3. ACh crosses cleft, binds NICOTINIC ACh RECEPTORS on motor end plate
4. receptors open → Na+ enters, K+ exits (Na+ dominates) → local depolarization = END PLATE POTENTIAL
5. end plate potential triggers action potential that propagates across sarcolemma
6. ACETYLCHOLINESTERASE (AChE) in the cleft breaks down ACh → stops the signal

excitation_contraction_coupling.what: linking the action potential to Ca2+ release and cross-bridge cycling.
steps: 1. action potential travels along sarcolemma → down T-TUBULES into the fiber
2. T-tubule voltage sensors (DHP RECEPTORS) mechanically open RYANODINE RECEPTORS on SR terminal cisternae
3. Ca2+ floods out of SR into sarcoplasm
4. Ca2+ binds TROPONIN → troponin shifts tropomyosin OFF myosin-binding sites on actin
6. when AP stops → Ca2+ pumped BACK into SR (Ca2+-ATPase) → tropomyosin recovers binding sites → contraction ends

not_yet_covered_in_class.note: these topics are ch9 but may not have been reached yet in lecture. fill in when prof covers them.

steps: 1. CROSS-BRIDGE FORMATION: energized myosin head binds actin (ADP + Pi still attached)
2. POWER STROKE: myosin head pivots, pulling actin toward M line. ADP + Pi released.
3. CROSS-BRIDGE DETACHMENT: new ATP binds myosin head → head detaches from actin. (NO ATP = no detachment = rigor mortis)
4. COCKING: ATP hydrolyzed to ADP + Pi → energy cocks the myosin head back to high-energy position. ready to bind again.
cycle repeats as long as Ca2+ is present and ATP is available.

isotonic.concentric: muscle SHORTENS under load. bicep curl UP. the work.
isotonic.eccentric: muscle LENGTHENS under load. bicep curl DOWN. where soreness comes from (micro-tears).

contraction_types.isometric: muscle generates force but does NOT change length. pushing against a wall. holding a heavy object still.

motor_unit.what: one motor neuron + ALL the muscle fibers it innervates.
motor_unit.small: fine control (eye muscles). few fibers per neuron.
motor_unit.large: power (quads, glutes). many fibers per neuron.
motor_unit.recruitment: as load increases, more motor units activated. smallest first (size principle).

twitch_summation_tetanus.twitch: single stimulus → single contraction-relaxation cycle. three phases: latent period (no visible contraction), contraction, relaxation.
twitch_summation_tetanus.wave_summation: repeated stimuli before full relaxation → forces ADD UP. stronger contraction.
twitch_summation_tetanus.incomplete_tetanus: visible relaxation between stimuli but forces accumulate.
twitch_summation_tetanus.complete_tetanus: no relaxation between stimuli. sustained max contraction. this is how normal movement works.

immediate.mechanism: CP donates phosphate to ADP → quick ATP. creatine kinase enzyme.

glycolytic.mechanism: anaerobic glycolysis. glucose → 2 pyruvate → lactic acid (when O2 is low). 2 net ATP per glucose.
glycolytic.byproduct: lactic acid → contributes to muscle fatigue + burning.

oxidative.source: glucose, fatty acids, (amino acids at extreme)
oxidative.mechanism: aerobic respiration. glycolysis → krebs cycle → electron transport chain → CO2 + H2O + ~36 ATP per glucose.

not_yet_covered_in_class.rigor_mortis: after death: ATP production stops → myosin heads can't detach from actin → all muscles lock rigid. lasts ~24-48 hours until proteins degrade.

muscle_fatigue.causes: ATP depletion, lactic acid accumulation, ionic imbalance (K+ leak from fibers), SR Ca2+ handling failure.
muscle_fatigue.NOT_just_lactic_acid: the old 'lactic acid causes fatigue' model is incomplete. multiple factors contribute.

not_yet_covered_in_class.length_tension_relationship: muscle generates maximum force when sarcomeres are at optimal resting length (optimal actin-myosin overlap). too stretched = not enough overlap = weak. too compressed = thick filaments hit Z discs = weak.
